correctness.rationale: With strict remainders Hamilton is represented by floor(h p_i+α_h) with a common α_h in (0,1). If a party loses a seat, its adjusted quota decreases by less than one, and parties with no larger share cannot gain. Each of the other parties can gain at most one, so both must gain and the loser is the smallest. The smallest cannot hold a seat at h≤2, since the ordered allocations are monotone in share. At h=3 a loss must start from (1,1,1), ending at (2,2,0). The h=4 middle-party remainder comparison gives v−u>1/4 and hence u<1/6. The h=3 largest party must then have w<1/2 (otherwise it already has at least two floors or its remainder exceeds 3u). Thus v>1/3, the three- and four-seat floor vectors both equal (1,1,0), and the h=3 comparison is w−u<1/3. Conversely these strict comparisons give both claimed allocations. The ordered triangle has area 1/864: its u-limits are 1/9 and 1/6 with split at 5/36 into two triangles of area 1/1728 each. Density 2 and six labeled chambers give 1/72. Exact quota/remainder boundaries are a null set. A separate arrangement calculation (python3 /workspace/audit_evidence/apportionment.py) partitioned one chamber into 44 open cells, directly tested each of the three enlargements by exact quota-error minimization, and checked the inequalities and summed loss areas 0,0,1/864. No finite population grid is used to prove the continuum claim.
